chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: O son of Adam, you do not treat Me justly. I draw near to you with blessings, while you draw near to Me with sins. My goodness descends upon you, and your evil rises up to Me. And yet, a noble angel comes to Me from you every day and night with an ugly deed. O son of Adam, if you were to hear your description from anyone else, not knowing that it was about you, you would rush to despise him.
ai.seo_question: What does God say about the imbalance between His blessings and human sins in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, emphasizes the theological concept of divine generosity (fayd) versus human ingratitude, illustrating how God’s blessings descend while human sins ascend for accountability. It serves as a profound psychological insight into human vanity, using the metaphor of hearing an external critique to highlight the disconnect between self-perception and actual spiritual state. In Shia tradition, this underscores the necessity of self-reflection (muhasaba) and humility before the continuous flow of divine grace.
